caption: The drawing contains three distinct objects arranged on a plain, slightly yellowed background. At the top, there is a large, rectangular textile sample featuring an elaborate floral and avian pattern. The textile’s colors are primarily black and white, with areas accented in red and pink. The design includes large, blooming flowers with detailed petals and leaves, surrounded by ornate foliage and scrollwork. Toward the center, two birds appear perched in a mirrored pose, facing each other and surrounded by additional flowers, contributing to an oval-shaped medallion. Below this textile, on the left, is a smaller, irregularly shaped swatch that replicates a section of the main textile’s pattern, showing a prominent red/pink flower with detailed leaves and smaller blossoms. On the lower right is a black-and-white drawing of a bird, possibly an eagle, standing atop a floral arrangement and clutching a shield with vertical stripes. Above this bird is a flowing banner with the partially legible motto “PLUR UNUM.” A signature reading “James Voss” is located beneath the eagle.
title: Textile Drapery
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
